description: Ad-hoc filter behaviour of the relations tooltip footer against the LGTM stack's own service graph, which Tempo's metrics-generator publishes with real client/server labels. Sibling of echarts-relations-adhoc-filters on the dev Grafana; same six panels, a topology small enough to hold in your head. Grafana and Prometheus sit in the middle, user is a pure origin, elasticsearch and grafana-assistant-app are pure destinations, and prometheus calls itself.

links.title: The rest of the LGTM relations dashboards

options.content:
# Ad hoc filters for relations

Pin a tooltip by selecting a node or edge. If the field is filterable, the tooltip can add or remove an ad hoc filter.

The panel writes filters to the Ad hoc filters variable at the top of this dashboard. Prometheus applies the variable to the metric selectors.

An edge can use `source` and `target` as display labels while the query uses different label keys. Keep the original labels in the query result so the panel can detect their names.

The examples use these cases:

| Panel | Case |
| --- | --- |
| 2 | Filterable fields and derived nodes |
| 3 | Fields that are not filterable |
| 4 | Source and target direction for node filters |
| 5 | A derived node with no matching field |
| 6 | Different endpoint labels in one graph |
| 7 | Copied endpoint labels with automatic name detection |

Clear the Ad hoc filters variable before you compare panels. An existing filter changes the data in every panel.

panels.title: The gate is on — and every node here is derived
panels.description:
The query groups the metric by `client` and `server`. The panel recognizes this endpoint pair and uses the same keys for filters.

The query returns edge fields only. The panel derives each node from the edge endpoints, and the node uses the filterable state of those edges.

Select an edge to filter by `client`, `server`, or `connection_type`.

panels.title: The same panel with Filterable off — no buttons at all
panels.description:
This panel uses the same query as panel 2, but Filterable is off. Node and edge tooltips do not offer ad hoc filter actions.

Data links use separate field configuration. Turning Filterable off does not turn data links off.

panels.title: Direction — a destination-only node asserts its target key
panels.description:
A node filter uses the endpoint labels for the edges that touch the node. Select `elasticsearch` to create a `server` filter because it appears only as a target.

Select `grafana` to create a `client` filter because it appears as a source. The panel does not create an either-endpoint filter.

Filter out this value excludes the node from both endpoint keys. This prevents the node from returning through the other direction.

panels.title: Why the fallback exists — a node override with nothing to bind to
panels.description:
The query returns edges but no node fields. The panel derives the `elasticsearch` node from the edge endpoints.

A field override can match only a field that exists before the panel renders it. If no node field exists, the derived node uses the filterable state of its edges.

Turn Filterable off for the edge fields if no mark in the panel must offer filter actions.

panels.title: Two levels in one frame, each filtering under its own keys
panels.description:
This graph combines two endpoint pairs. Level 1 uses `stack` and `client`, while level 2 uses `client` and `server`.

The query keeps the original labels after it adds `source` and `target`. The panel can therefore recover the correct filter keys for each edge.

The `grafana` node appears in both levels. Its connected edges resolve to one `client` filter key.

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target, stack, client) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "stack", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "client", "(.*)")
)
or
sum by (source, target, client, server) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)")
)

panels.title: Copied endpoints: original labels provide the filter names
panels.description:
This query copies `client` and `server` to `source` and `target`. The outer aggregation also keeps the original labels.

The panel matches the endpoint values to the original labels. It then uses `client` and `server` as the ad hoc filter names without manual configuration.

targets.expr:
sum by (source, target, client, server) (
  label_replace(
    label_replace(
      rate(traces_service_graph_request_total{client!="", server!=""}[$__range]),
    "source", "$1", "client", "(.*)"),
  "target", "$1", "server", "(.*)")
)
